parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  Planet Earth is home to many different climate zones. A climate zone is a region of the world where the weather follows a regular pattern throughout the year.
content: 📖 Planet Earth is home to many different climate zones. A climate zone is a region of the world where the weather follows a regular pattern throughout the year.

The tropical zone, found near the equator, is hot and wet all year round. Rainforests grow here because they receive over 2,000 mm of rainfall every year. In contrast, the desert zone is extremely hot and dry. The Sahara Desert in Africa receives less than 250 mm of rain per year.

The temperate zone, where many people live, has four seasons: spring, summer, autumn, and winter. Temperatures are mild — not too hot and not too cold. Northern Europe and much of North America fall into this zone.
At the poles, the polar zone is the coldest place on Earth. In winter, temperatures in Antarctica can drop below -60°C. Very few plants or animals can survive there.
Understanding climate zones helps scientists predict weather, plan farming, and understand how climate change is affecting our world.
